what: The Salary Calculator converts pay from one period to all the others. Type an amount and choose whether it is per hour, day, week, month or year, and the tool shows your hourly, daily, weekly, every-2-weeks, monthly and yearly pay at once.

It is handy when you compare a job offer given as an hourly rate with one given as a yearly salary, when you plan a monthly budget from an hourly wage, or when you want to know your real hourly rate on a fixed salary. You can set your own hours per week, days per week and weeks per year.
The results are gross pay, before tax and deductions, and everything is calculated in your browser. Results are estimates and not financial advice.
uses: Turn an hourly offer and a yearly offer into the same unit so you can compare them fairly.
Convert an hourly wage to a monthly amount to plan rent and bills.
Enter a yearly salary and your real hours to see what you earn per hour.
Lower the hours per week or days per week to see part-time pay.
Reduce the weeks per year to see the effect of unpaid weeks.
tutorial: Enter a number in "Pay amount", for example 25. The default is 25 per hour.
In "Per", choose Hour, Day, Week, Month or Year to say what your amount covers.
Set "Hours per week" (1 to 168), "Days per week" (1 to 7) and "Weeks per year" (1 to 52). The defaults are 40, 5 and 52.
The boxes show "Hourly", "Daily", "Weekly", "Every 2 weeks", "Monthly" and "Yearly" pay. They all update when you change any field.
The note under the results says these are before tax and deductions. Your take-home pay will be lower.
features: First the tool finds yearly pay: hourly × hours per week × weeks; daily × days per week × weeks; weekly × weeks; monthly × 12. Then it divides that yearly total back into each period.
Hourly, daily, weekly, every 2 weeks, monthly and yearly.
Change hours, days and weeks to match your real job.
Biweekly pay is weekly pay × 2, useful if you are paid every other Friday.
Monthly pay is yearly pay ÷ 12, so it is the same every month.

example.title: Worked example: 22 per hour
example.text: You earn 22 per hour, work 40 hours a week, 5 days a week, 52 weeks a year. Yearly pay is 22 × 40 × 52 = 45,760.00. The tool shows Daily 176.00, Weekly 880.00, Every 2 weeks 1,760.00 and Monthly 3,813.33. Now try a 55000 salary with "Per" set to Year and the same pattern: Hourly is 26.44, Weekly is 1,057.69 and Monthly is 4,583.33.

tips: If you take 2 weeks of unpaid leave, set "Weeks per year" to 50.
If you are paid on a salary but work long hours, enter your real hours to see your true hourly rate.
Daily pay depends on "Days per week", so a 4-day, 40-hour week gives a higher daily figure.
Monthly is yearly ÷ 12, not weekly × 4, because most months are a little longer than 4 weeks.
Use a tax calculator for your country to estimate take-home pay from these gross figures.
problems: All results show a dash and a red message
The message says which box to fix: the pay amount must be above 0, hours per week up to 168 (and no more than 24 × days per week), days per week up to 7 and weeks per year up to 52.
Monthly pay is more than 4 × weekly pay
That is correct. A year has 52 weeks, which is about 4.33 weeks per month.
Changing hours does nothing when I enter a yearly salary
Hours only change the hourly figure for a salary. Weekly, monthly and yearly pay stay the same.
My paycheck is smaller than the result
The tool shows gross pay. Tax, insurance and other deductions are taken out of your real paycheck.
